key_insight: The LLM adapts neural operators using both a task-dependent prior and real-time experimental feedback, rather than relying on either alone.
engineering_relevance: This suggests LLM-based hyperparameter or configuration search can outperform random search and Bayesian optimization in transfer settings, potentially reducing tuning cost for PDE surrogate models.
method: LLM selects fine-tuning configurations for neural operators under a limited trial budget.
Compare transfers within and across PDE families against random search and Bayesian optimization.
Use controlled interventions to separate initial task bias from responses to validation feedback.
evidence_signal: Across matched comparisons, the LLM achieved lower held-out test nRMSE than random search and Bayesian optimization in nearly every case, and intervention tests showed its next proposal changed when validation scores were reassigned.
watch_item: The findings depend on controlled benchmark-style interventions, so real-world gains may vary when feedback is noisy, sparse, or differently structured.
paper_title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
